name: Borrow Checkers Kochi
tagline: Rust and systems programming in Kochi: small talks, real code, strong coffee.
about:
Borrow Checkers Kochi started in early 2023 as six people arguing about lifetimes over filter coffee at a bakery in Kadavanthra. We now meet once a month at a cowork in Panampilly Nagar, and the arguments have turned into talks, workshops and a fair amount of shared code.

We're for anyone who writes software close to the metal, or wants to: Rust beginners staring at their first ownership error, embedded tinkerers blinking LEDs on a microcontroller, backend engineers chasing tail latency, and the occasional C veteran who came to heckle and stayed. No talk is too small. The five-minute lightning slot is where most of our regulars gave their first talk.

Every meetup has a beginner track, one deep-dive talk and an hour of open hacking. Between meetups we run a Thursday-night study group and a mentoring programme that pairs first-time open-source contributors with someone who has shipped a crate.

The house rules are short. Be kind about other people's code, explain your acronyms, and wash your own cup.

events.name: Rust from Zero: Ownership Weekend

venue.name: Thuruthu Coworks
venue.address: 2nd floor, 41/1180 Panampilly Avenue, Panampilly Nagar, Kochi 682036

events.about:
A full Saturday for people who have heard Rust is hard and would like to find out for themselves. We start from cargo new and finish with a small command-line tool that reads the ferry timetable between Fort Kochi and Vypin and tells you when the next boat leaves. Along the way: ownership, borrowing, enums, pattern matching and the compiler errors that teach you more than any slide.

The morning is explanation and live coding; the afternoon is pair programming with one mentor for every six people. The fee covers Kerala meals from the canteen downstairs, tea twice and a printed cheat sheet.

You don't need any systems programming background. You do need to have written a loop and a function in some language, and to be fine with being confused for about forty minutes before it clicks.
events.guidelines: Bring a laptop with Rust installed through rustup (we email a setup checklist two days before) and your charger, because power strips are limited. Arrive by 9:45 so we can start on time. Pairs are mixed on purpose, so expect to sit with someone new. Photos are taken in the afternoon; tell the front desk if you'd rather not be in them.

speakers.bio: Rewrote a billing service in Rust at a Kakkanad SaaS company and spent the following year explaining why. Has taught this workshop five times.

speakers.bio: Moved a ledger service from Java to Rust in 2024 and explains the borrow checker with drawings of house keys and who is holding them.

events.name: Meetup #27: Async Without Tears

venue.name: Thuruthu Coworks
venue.address: 2nd floor, 41/1180 Panampilly Avenue, Panampilly Nagar, Kochi 682036

events.about:
Our monthly meetup, this time on async Rust: what an executor actually does, why your future isn't running, and how to stop holding a lock across an await. The main talk walks through a job runner that moves parcels for a logistics company, and the three outages that shaped it.

Before that, the beginner track spends twenty minutes explaining futures with a dosa counter: you hand over a token, go do something else, and someone shouts your number. After the talks we break into open hacking, and the study group will be at the back table for anyone stuck on the concurrency chapter.
events.guidelines: Free, but please RSVP so we order enough snacks. Doors open at 6:15 and the first talk starts at 6:45 sharp. If you RSVP and can't make it, cancel from the app so someone on the waitlist gets your seat.

speakers.name: Arun Thekkekara
speakers.bio: Maintains an async job runner that moves a few million parcels a week across South India. Collects outage stories the way other people collect stamps.

speakers.name: Meghna Iyer
speakers.bio: Gave her first lightning talk here in 2024. Now runs the beginner track and explains concurrency with breakfast food.

agenda.title: Beginner track: futures at the dosa counter
Async without tears: three outages and a job runner

Arun's second outage story was painfully familiar. Great talk.
The room got very warm after eight. A second fan would help.
Loved the lightning talk on cancelling tasks safely. Short and sharp.

events.name: Embedded Rust Night: Blink, Then Think

venue.name: Pattam Makerspace
venue.address: Ground floor, Kalamassery Startup Arcade, HMT Road, Kalamassery, Kochi 683503

events.about:
A hands-on evening with a ₹450 microcontroller board, a breadboard and a bag of LEDs. We start by blinking an LED with no operating system underneath, then read a temperature sensor, then put the numbers on a tiny OLED screen. Everyone goes home with a board that shows the room temperature and their name.

The fee covers the kit, which is yours to keep. The talk portion is short: Fathima explains what no_std means and why the compiler suddenly cares about panics, and Vimal shows the soil moisture sensor he ships to spice farms in Wayanad, which runs on the same board.

Seats were capped at thirty so every table had a mentor. If you missed it, we'll run it again early next year.
events.guidelines: Bring a laptop that takes a USB cable (we have USB-C adapters). Install the toolchain from the emailed checklist the day before; flashing drivers on Windows take a while. Please don't connect anything to a powered board until a mentor has checked your wiring.

speakers.name: Fathima Rizvana
speakers.bio: Writes firmware for medical devices and has a strong opinion about every pull-up resistor in the room.

speakers.name: Vimal Krishnadas
speakers.bio: Builds soil moisture sensors for spice farms in Wayanad. Moved the firmware from C to Rust after a memory bug cost a whole monsoon of data.

agenda.title: Sensors, the I2C bus and a tiny screen
Field story: a monsoon of lost data

One mentor per table made all the difference. Nobody got left behind.

Vimal's monsoon story is the best argument for Rust I've heard.

events.name: Meetup #29: Profiling in Production

venue.name: Thuruthu Coworks
venue.address: 2nd floor, 41/1180 Panampilly Avenue, Panampilly Nagar, Kochi 682036

events.about:
This month is about finding out where the time goes. Leena walks through flame graphs from a real service: an endpoint that took 900 milliseconds, the allocation storm behind it, and the three-line change that brought it down to 40. You'll see how to profile a release build without shipping debug symbols, and how to read a flame graph without squinting.

The beginner track covers benchmarking honestly: why your first benchmark lies to you, and how to write one that doesn't. Lightning talks are open as always; claim a slot in the RSVP form.
events.guidelines: Free entry; please RSVP so we can plan chairs and snacks. Doors open at 6:15. The talks are recorded for the club page, so tell us at the door if you'd rather sit out of frame. Bring a laptop if you want to try the profiling exercise during open hacking.

speakers.name: Leena Mathews
speakers.bio: Reads flame graphs for a living at a Kochi logistics company and once traced a two-second delay to a single misplaced clone.

speakers.name: Harish Gopal
speakers.bio: Lost a week to a benchmark that measured the wrong thing. Now teaches everyone else how not to.

events.name: First PR Saturday
events.about:
A day for opening your first pull request to a Rust project. Beforehand, our mentors collect around forty beginner-friendly issues from crates they know well: documentation fixes, missing tests, small improvements to error messages. On the day you pick one, a mentor pairs with you on a call, and you push your PR before dinner.

It's online so people from Kozhikode, Thrissur and further away can join in. There's a shared voice room for questions and a progress board where every opened PR gets a crab next to it.
events.guidelines: You'll need git, a working Rust setup and a GitHub account. Mentors send the issue list on the Thursday before; reply with your top three picks. Be gentle with maintainers: one issue per person until your first PR has been reviewed. Cameras are optional, microphones are encouraged.

events.name: Systems Weekend at Vagamon
events.about:
Two days in the hills with twenty-four people and no slide on screen for longer than ten minutes. Together we build a tiny key-value store from scratch: a write-ahead log on Saturday, compaction and crash recovery on Sunday. Evenings are for a bonfire and the kind of conversations that never happen in a co-working space.

The fee covers a shared room for one night, four meals, the bus from Kaloor and back, and a great deal of tea. It sold out in two days; join the waitlist if you'd like a seat at the next one.
events.guidelines: The bus leaves Kaloor at 6:00 on Saturday and is back by 8:00 on Sunday night. Pack warm clothes, because Vagamon gets cold after dark. Bring a laptop and charger; the power is reliable but the internet isn't, so download the crate docs before you leave.
